owner: semantic plan Task 10 / profile plan Task 6 (Release-A evaluation step)
purpose: Replay/fixture gold set for the Release-A semantic-context evaluation. NO live catalog rows and NO live provider: every column below is a self-contained fixture (a CanonicalRow plus an optional GlossaryRecord sidecar) that the REAL Pass-A enrichment payload builders can be driven over.
how_the_oracle_works: Each case names the concept a human reviewer expects (`expected_concept`) and the concept the SAME question collapses to when the disambiguating context is absent (`confusable_concept`). The replay oracle inspects the payload the pipeline ACTUALLY built for the column and answers `expected_concept` only when the `discriminator` is satisfied by that payload. The discriminator therefore measures ONE thing: does the rich (v4/flag-on) path put the disambiguating evidence in front of the model where the thin (v1/flag-off) path does not. It deliberately does NOT model provider skill -- that is Gate B.

discriminator_modes.requires_any: answer `expected_concept` iff at least one listed term appears in the serialized payload; otherwise `confusable_concept`.
discriminator_modes.requires_absent: answer `expected_concept` iff NONE of the listed payload KEYS is present; otherwise `confusable_concept`. Used by the honestly-unclassified family, where the correct behaviour is to decline rather than to invent.

invariants_enforced_by_the_self_check: every `expected_concept`/`confusable_concept`/`acceptable_concepts` member is a real registry concept or the literal 'unclassified'
every `requires_any` discriminator term IS present in the rich payload and IS NOT present in the thin payload (otherwise the eval would be tautological or vacuous)
every family carries at least one `case` and at least one `counterexample`
the six named CIB/FTR witnesses are present as fixture columns
no two cases share a (table, column)

families.defect: A counterparty's SWIFT bank code read as the bank's own customer-file identifier (or the reverse). The two live in DISJOINT identifier namespaces (swift_bic vs cif), so the conflation manufactures a cross-namespace join.

glossary.definition: The SWIFT Business Identifier Code of the counterparty bank on the transaction.
glossary.bian_path: Party Reference Data Directory > Party Routing Profile

discriminator.why: the roster proves a SEPARATE CIF column exists on this same table, and `related_terms` names the bank leg -- neither reaches the thin payload

glossary.definition: The bank's own customer information file identifier for the counterparty.
glossary.bian_path: Party Reference Data Directory > Customer Identification

discriminator.why: the roster proves a SEPARATE BIC column carries the bank code; the process path is an onboarding path, not a payment-routing path

families.defect: A beneficiary account reference at another institution read as an account in our own ledger. Same defect shape as BIC/CIF: internal_account and external_account are disjoint namespaces.

glossary.definition: The account number held at the receiving institution to which the funds are credited.

discriminator.why: the roster proves the OWN-LEDGER debit account is a different column; `related_terms` names the foreign institution

glossary.definition: The account on this bank's core ledger that the transaction is debited from.

discriminator.why: the roster proves the FOREIGN account is a different column; the process path is a core-ledger path

families.defect: An all-digit settlement amount read as a serial number, or a numeric core-banking serial read as money. Attributing money to an identifier column is the acceptance path for a silently wrong feature.

glossary.definition: The settled amount transferred to the counterparty on this transaction.

discriminator.why: a sibling currency column and a currency related-term are what make a bare decimal MONEY rather than a serial

glossary.definition: The monotonically increasing serial the core banking system assigns to each posting.

discriminator.why: a reconciliation process path and a system related-term separate a numeric SERIAL from a numeric AMOUNT

families.defect: The live conflation the concept critic exists for: a free-text branch DESCRIPTION classified as the branch IDENTIFIER, which then offers a description column as a join key.

glossary.definition: The free-text description of the service outlet (branch) that booked the transaction.
glossary.bian_path: Party Reference Data Directory > Service Outlet

discriminator.why: the roster proves the branch IDENTIFIER is a different column, so this varchar(200) is the label, not the key

glossary.definition: The code identifying the service outlet that booked the transaction.
glossary.bian_path: Party Reference Data Directory > Service Outlet

discriminator.why: the roster proves the free-text label is a different column, so this varchar(8) is the key

families.defect: A business event date read as a system/load timestamp (or the reverse). Point-in-time correctness dies here: a feature cut on the load time leaks the future.

glossary.definition: The business date on which the transaction was posted to the ledger.

discriminator.why: the roster proves the LOAD timestamp is a different column, so this date is the business event

glossary.definition: The wall-clock time at which this row landed in the compliance extract.

discriminator.why: the roster proves the BUSINESS date is a different column; the process path is an ingestion path

families.defect: A three-character currency denomination read as the monetary value it denominates (or the reverse). Aggregating the currency column, or summing across denominations, both follow.

glossary.definition: The ISO-4217 currency the transaction amount is denominated in.

discriminator.why: the roster proves the AMOUNT is a different column, so this char(3) denominates rather than measures

glossary.definition: The transaction value converted into the booking entity's reporting currency.

discriminator.why: the roster proves the CURRENCY is a different column, so this decimal is the value

families.defect: A coded status and its human-readable label conflated. The label is then offered as a groupable state, and the code as prose.

glossary.definition: The coded settlement state of the transaction at extract time.

discriminator.why: the roster proves the LABEL is a different column, so this char(2) is the state itself

glossary.definition: The human-readable rendering of the coded settlement state.

discriminator.why: the roster proves the CODE is a different column, so this varchar(120) is its rendering

families.defect: Two failure directions, and both are graded here: a personal attribute NOT recognized as sensitive (it then flows into an egress payload), and an ordinary commercial attribute OVER-flagged as protected (a real column is then withheld for no reason).

glossary.definition: The birth date recorded for the natural person on the customer file.
glossary.bian_path: Party Reference Data Directory > Party Profile

discriminator.why: an identity-verification process path and a natural-person related-term are what make this DATE a person, not a timestamp

glossary.definition: The ISO country code of the citizenship declared by the customer.
glossary.bian_path: Party Reference Data Directory > Party Profile

discriminator.why: nationality is a protected characteristic; without the related-term this reads as an ordinary geography code

glossary.definition: The commercial portfolio segment the relationship is managed under.

discriminator.why: a commercial segmentation path is what keeps a per-customer code from being over-flagged as a protected characteristic

families.defect: An outcome recorded AFTER the decision, used as an input feature. The counterexample guards the opposite error: an ordinary operational flag treated as a label and needlessly withheld.

glossary.definition: Set when an investigation concluded and a regulatory report was filed for this transaction.

discriminator.why: the OUTCOME process path is the only signal that this flag is set after the fact -- a leakage anchor, not an input

glossary.definition: Set when the posting is shown on the customer's statement.

discriminator.why: a delivery-preference path is what stops an ordinary presentation flag from being quarantined as a target

families.defect: Two directions again. A column with no meaning at all must come back `unclassified` rather than pattern-matched from its name; a column whose meaning only the RICH context carries must not be dismissed as opaque.

discriminator.why: no meaning-bearing key exists for this column in EITHER mode, so the honest answer is to decline. The measurement this makes falsifiable: the rich adapter must not FABRICATE a meaning-bearing key out of the sibling roster or the table context.
an opaque name whose leading token invites an `account`/`a1` guess; nothing in either payload licenses one

glossary.definition: The fee levied on the payer for executing this transfer.

discriminator.why: the fee process path is what turns an abbreviated four-letter name into a known monetary flow; without it the honest answer really is `unclassified`, and THAT is the precision cost the thin baseline pays

cross_namespace_pairs.purpose: The `zero BIC<->CIF candidates` release bar, and the `false cross-namespace candidates` per-family metric. Each entry names two gold columns and whether the platform may EVER offer them as an identifier-link candidate. Evaluated against the real grounding assessor, not a re-implementation.

must_not_pair.why: swift_bic and cif are disjoint registries; equal values would be a coincidence
external_account vs internal_account -- the same defect one level down
a DESCRIPTION is never an identifier endpoint, even for the same branch

may_pair.why: same cif registry, same issuer -- the positive control that proves the gate is not simply refusing everything

peer_catalog.purpose: A SECOND catalog source so cross-catalog pairing has something to pair with. Only the columns the cross-namespace controls reference.

glossary.definition: The customer information file identifier on the customer master.
glossary.bian_path: Party Reference Data Directory > Customer Identification

glossary.definition: The SWIFT Business Identifier Code of the institution where this customer banks.
glossary.bian_path: Party Reference Data Directory > Party Routing Profile

retrieval_questions.purpose: Grounded-retrieval hit rate and the thin-vs-rich retrieval lift. A hit is a retrieved object ref that appears in `expected_refs`; `forbidden_refs` are objects whose retrieval for this question is a defect, not a miss.

questions.question: how much did we actually settle to the counterparty, and in what currency
what bank is the counterparty at
when was the transaction posted to the ledger
what account at the receiving institution did the money go to
which transactions ended in a filed regulatory report

unsafe_features.purpose: The `zero unsafe gold features accepted` release bar. Each entry is a feature a generator might propose over these columns; `unsafe` ones must never be accepted as design-checked.
